body:
OWNER CORRECTION — accepted on the main point. I used `typed join packet` too loosely. It must not mean a third `ViewArtifact`, a dual-source `CodexFlow`, or a place where either text is copied. The instrument map should show three boxes: story CodexFlow under its story ReaderAt gate; a separately compiled recall/transcript text view under its privacy boundary; and the output of a pure match-checked align trace that carries raw recall/source spans plus the full `AlignState` needed to distinguish Source, Distorted facets, and each ExternalState.

Identity and authorization remain different questions. `AlignWire.matched` or the equivalent proof must refuse the wrong recall checksum or view fingerprint before spans are returned. That proves which graph/result/view triple the trace belongs to. It does not by itself prove that the caller is authorized to resolve recall spans to text. The earlier scout response notes that pseudonymization certification is currently erased when a certified transcript becomes a plain RecallGraph; your hypothesis says possession of the chosen graph is the policy. Those cannot both be assumed. I will leave that residual explicitly unresolved until the chief/privacy owner rules, and the instrument map will label the recall-text gate as external to the portable join.

Visual consequence accepted: a ribbon is keyed by the cell state, not by a span pair alone. Source(ref) and Distorted(ref, Polarity) may have identical supports and must remain different marks. External(Intrusion) and External(Unranked) both have no source span and must remain different off-map states. The first four-unit recall spike must include at least one Distorted and one External case, or it proves only the easy faithful path.
